approachQuestion.prompt:
A W-bit permission word M specifies which permissions are eligible. Return all words s whose set positions are a subset of the set positions in M, including zero, in strictly decreasing numeric order.

Constraints: 1 <= W <= 64; M has k set bits, 0 <= k <= min(W,20). Return an array of words.
Example: W=4, M=10 -> [10,8,2,0]. Edge case: M=0 -> [0].

Choose the best approach under these constraints.
constraints: W and k are parameters. W-bit subtraction wraps modulo 2^W. Bit operations and appending one word to the output take constant amortized time; output allocation is excluded from auxiliary storage.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

options.text: Start s=M and emit s. If s is zero, stop; otherwise replace s with (s-1) AND M and repeat.
options.feedback: Subtracting crosses to the next eligible pattern when forbidden positions are masked away. Stopping at zero prevents cycling back to M.

options.text: Scan every W-bit value from the maximum down to zero and emit it exactly when (value AND M) equals value, using a nonwrapping loop counter.
options.feedback: This emits exactly the right words in order but tests values involving permissions outside M.

options.text: Emit M, then repeatedly XOR the current word with M until it reaches zero.
options.feedback: For M=10, this emits only 10 and 0, skipping 8 and 2.

options.text: Run the same (s-1) AND M transition, stopping before emitting zero.
options.feedback: Zero is a valid subset. For M=0 the required output is [0], not an empty array.

feedback.reason: Subtract one then mask with M skips to the next smaller eligible submask.
details: Emit the current submask and stop immediately after emitting zero. For each nonzero current submask, subtract one and mask with M to reach the next smaller allowed word. No output copy or recursion is used.

Subtract one then mask with M skips to the next smaller eligible submask. Emit zero and stop before decrementing it, or modular underflow would restart enumeration. Output has 2^k values even for sparse positions in M.

“Start s=M and emit s. If s is zero, stop; otherwise replace s with (s-1) AND M and repeat.”: Subtracting crosses to the next eligible pattern when forbidden positions are masked away. Stopping at zero prevents cycling back to M.

“Scan every W-bit value from the maximum down to zero and emit it exactly when (value AND M) equals value, using a nonwrapping loop counter.”: This emits exactly the right words in order but tests values involving permissions outside M.
“Emit M, then repeatedly XOR the current word with M until it reaches zero.”: For M=10, this emits only 10 and 0, skipping 8 and 2.
“Run the same (s-1) AND M transition, stopping before emitting zero.”: Zero is a valid subset. For M=0 the required output is [0], not an empty array.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For descending-submask-step, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let k be the number of set bits in M. Include writing the returned array in time, but exclude that array from auxiliary space.
constraints: W and k are parameters. W-bit subtraction wraps modulo 2^W. Bit operations and appending one word to the output take constant amortized time; output allocation is excluded from auxiliary storage.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

feedback.reason: Emit each eligible submask once with fixed scalar state.
details: Each of the 2^k submasks is emitted once using constant word work and amortized append cost. Only M and the current submask are retained outside the returned array.
W and k are parameters. W-bit subtraction wraps modulo 2^W. Bit operations and appending one word to the output take constant amortized time; output allocation is excluded from auxiliary storage.
“O(2^W) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This is scanning all W-bit values; the analyzed method visits only submasks.
“O(2^k) time, O(2^k) auxiliary space”: The returned array is explicitly excluded and no second array is built.
“O(k) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: There are 2^k output words even though the input uses one word.
